For s>1, J′=(1+as)^−d∈(0,1), so 2s−J increases from a negative value and tends to infinity; the positive region is terminal. On it the quotient derivative numerator is at most 2−J(1)<0 by concavity. The concave function (d+1)x−2x^d is at least d−1 throughout x∈[(d−1)/d,1] by its two endpoint values and (1+1/(d−1))^(d−1)≥2. Hence G(1)≥1−v*. Since G has at most an increase followed by a decrease and tends to −∞, its sign on [R,∞) changes at most once from plus to minus. Thus N′ is bounded below by the lesser of N′(R) and its limit A≥0.
